statusConventions: field/alias/value: absent = not declared (silently ignored), accepted = decoded, deprecated = decoded with a warning, rejected = config fails. constraint: accepted = a config breaking the rule still loads (or the rule does not exist in that tag), rejected = it fails to load or crashes the core, absent = the field the rule is about does not exist in that tag. perVersionKeys: null = the parent object is not declared in that tag. Checks enforced at core start (proxy constructors) rather than in infra/conf are called out in detail.

items.detail: Inbound protocol registry is identical in v26.3.27, v26.7.28 and v26.9.9, and v26.9.30 and v26.10.10 add masque; the name is lower-cased before lookup and any other name fails the whole config with "unknown config id".

Outbound protocol registry is identical in v26.3.27, v26.7.28 and v26.9.9, and v26.9.30 and v26.10.10 add masque; the name is lower-cased before lookup and any other name fails the whole config with "unknown config id".
"masque" is registered as an inbound and an outbound protocol from v26.9.30; in the three earlier tags a masque outbound fails to load with "unknown config id: masque".
"tunnel" and "dokodemo-door" share DokodemoConfig, and "mixed" and "socks" share SocksServerConfig, so each pair accepts identical settings in every tag.
"block"/"blackhole" and "direct"/"freedom" are pairs of names for the same settings struct in every tag.

A missing "settings" is decoded as {} in every tag, so it only fails when the protocol has a required field (vless decryption/encryption, hysteria version, wireguard secretKey, trojan/ss/vmess/vless server, etc.).

Settings are decoded with encoding/json, which matches keys case-insensitively, so e.g. "MTU"/"mtu" or "Clients"/"clients" all bind the same field; only spelling differences (not case) make a key unknown and silently ignored.

A missing "settings" is decoded as {} in every tag, so it only fails when the protocol has a required field (vless decryption/encryption, hysteria version, wireguard secretKey, trojan/ss/vmess/vless server, etc.).

Settings are decoded with encoding/json, which matches keys case-insensitively, so e.g. "MTU"/"mtu" or "Clients"/"clients" all bind the same field; only spelling differences (not case) make a key unknown and silently ignored.
Before v26.9.9 the response object is parsed by a sub-loader keyed on "type" (other keys ignored); v26.9.9 decodes it into a typed struct {type, customResponseData}.
Case-insensitive in every tag; "custom" exists only in v26.9.9, and any unlisted value fails the config ("unknown config id" before v26.9.9, "unknown blackhole response" in v26.9.9).
A response object without "type" (e.g. {}) fails with "type not found in JSON context" in v26.3.27/v26.7.28, but is treated as "none" in v26.9.9.
Only read when type is "custom"; must be standard (padded) base64, and a decode failure fails the config.
Same shape as inbound sniffing (enabled, destOverride, domainsExcluded, ipsExcluded, metadataOnly, routeOnly); an invalid destOverride or unparsable domain/IP rule fails the config.
Case-insensitive; https/ssl map to tls and fakedns+others maps to fakedns; any other entry fails the config with "unknown protocol".
Ordered list of {action, qType, domain, rCode}; first match wins, and with no match A/AAAA are hijacked and everything else gets an empty reply.
Case-insensitive and required: a missing or unlisted action fails the config with "unknown action".
rCode above 65535 fails the config; it is only meaningful with action "return".
Parsed as a port-list (number, "1,28" or "1-5" ranges expanded); an unparsable value fails JSON decoding.
Parsed with the routing domain-rule syntax where a bare string is a substring match; an invalid rule (e.g. bad regexp, missing geosite) fails the config.
From v26.7.28 its presence logs a deprecation warning and it is translated into equivalent "rules" (blockTypes rule, hijack A/AAAA, then a catch-all per mode).
Case-sensitive in every tag; "" means reject, and any other value fails the config.
Deprecated in favour of "rules" from v26.7.28, where each entry must also be 0..65535 or the config fails (v26.3.27 had no range check).
From v26.7.28, nonIPQuery or blockTypes together with any "rules" key (even an empty array) fails the config; v26.3.27 simply ignores "rules".
Default non-A/AAAA handling changed: v26.3.27 answers REFUSED (nonIPQuery defaults to reject), while from v26.7.28 a config with neither rules nor legacy keys returns an empty NOERROR reply.
New name for "network" from v26.7.28; v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
New name for "address" from v26.7.28; v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
New name for "port" from v26.7.28; v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
From v26.7.28 network/address/port are legacy aliases of rewriteNetwork/rewriteAddress/rewritePort and win whenever set (non-empty / non-zero); they are the only spelling v26.3.27 understands.
New name for "network" from v26.7.28 (also for protocol "tunnel"); v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
New name for "address" from v26.7.28 (also for protocol "tunnel"); v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
New name for "port" from v26.7.28 (also for protocol "tunnel"); v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
From v26.7.28 network/address/port are legacy aliases of allowedNetwork/rewriteAddress/rewritePort and win whenever set; only they work on v26.3.27.
Every portMap value must be "host:port" (host may be empty, e.g. ":80"); anything else fails the config with "invalid portMap".
When omitted only TCP is accepted; names other than tcp/udp/unix are not an error but become "unknown" and match nothing.

In v26.9.9 the freedom proxy no longer reads it: Build logs a deprecation warning and copies it into streamSettings.sockopt.domainStrategy, overwriting any sockopt.domainStrategy you set (and it is dropped if the outbound-level targetStrategy is non-AsIs).
settings.targetStrategy is an alias of settings.domainStrategy and wins when non-empty; in v26.9.9 both are deprecated together.
Case-insensitive ("" = asis); any other value fails the config with "unsupported domain strategy".
In v26.9.9 an outbound-level targetStrategy on a freedom outbound is moved to sockopt.domainStrategy with a warning and takes precedence over settings.domainStrategy.
v26.9.9 fails a freedom outbound whose sockopt.addressPortStrategy is anything but none/empty.
The singular "noise" object fails the config in every tag; use the "noises" array.
"tlshello" is case-insensitive and "" means all packets; otherwise it must parse as an integer range whose start is at least 1, or the config fails.
When fragment is present, length is required and its minimum must be at least 1, otherwise the config fails.
When fragment is present, interval is required (0 is allowed), otherwise the config fails.
Case-sensitive (no lower-casing) in every tag; any other value, including "Rand", fails the config.
For rand it must be an integer range with minimum at least 1; for hex it must decode as hex; for base64 it accepts std or URL alphabet with optional padding; a bad value fails the config.
Case-insensitive; "" and "all" mean ip; anything else fails the config.
Must be "host:port" (host may be empty) with a valid port, otherwise the config fails.
Only 1 and 2 are used; any other number is silently treated as 0 (off), not an error.
From v26.7.28 it only logs "has been removed and migrated to finalRules"; the value is not migrated and has no effect, and the config still loads.

First matching rule wins; after user rules an implicit rule blocks private IPs when the inbound is vless/vmess/trojan/hysteria/wireguard/shadowsocks (block-all for VLESS reverse). v26.9.9 ignores finalRules, with a warning, when sockopt.dialerProxy is set.
Case-insensitive and required: a missing or unlisted action fails the config with "unknown action".
Parsed with the routing IP-rule syntax (CIDR, geoip:...); an unparsable entry fails the config. network/port use the usual network-list and port-list forms.
Integer or "min-max" range applied before closing a blocked connection.
New spelling of "accounts" ({user, pass} items); v26.3.27 silently ignores it, leaving the inbound without authentication.
From v26.7.28 "accounts" wins over "users" whenever the key is present, even as an empty array.
Flat form (address, port, user, pass, level, email) replaces "servers" whenever address is set; otherwise servers[] is used.
servers must have exactly one entry and that entry at most one user, otherwise the config fails.
A server without address dereferences a nil pointer and crashes the core in v26.3.27/v26.7.28; v26.9.9 builds it with no address, so treat address as required everywhere.
Exact, case-sensitive match (also for "mixed"); any other value, e.g. "Password", silently falls back to noauth.
New spelling of "accounts" (also for "mixed"); v26.3.27 silently ignores it.
From v26.7.28 "accounts" wins over "users" whenever the key is present, even as an empty array.
Flat form (address, port, user, pass, level, email) replaces "servers" whenever address is set.
servers must have exactly one entry and that entry at most one user, otherwise the config fails.
A server without address crashes the core (nil pointer) in v26.3.27/v26.7.28 and builds an address-less endpoint in v26.9.9; treat it as required.
v26.3.27 decodes but never checks it; from v26.7.28 anything but 2 (including a missing key) fails the config with "version != 2".
Must be 2 in every tag; a missing or other value fails the config.
Missing address dereferences a nil pointer (core crash) in v26.3.27/v26.7.28; v26.9.9 builds an address-less endpoint. Treat as required.
New spelling of "clients" ({auth, level, email}); v26.3.27 silently ignores it, and from v26.7.28 "clients" wins whenever present, even empty.

Classic names are case-insensitive; "none"/"plain" were removed in v26.7.28 and now fail with "unknown cipher method"; 2022 names come from sing-shadowsocks v0.2.7 up to v26.9.9 (matched case-sensitively, with the base64 key only validated when the core starts) and, from v26.9.30, from the core's own shadowsocks_2022 package, which lower-cases the name first.

Classic names are case-insensitive; "none"/"plain" were removed in v26.7.28 and now fail with "unknown cipher method"; 2022 names come from sing-shadowsocks v0.2.7 up to v26.9.9 (matched case-sensitively, with the base64 key only validated when the core starts) and, from v26.9.30, from the core's own shadowsocks_2022 package, which lower-cases the name first.
For non-2022 multi-user inbounds each client method must be one of the AEAD ciphers; none/plain or unknown fails with "unsupported cipher method" in every tag.
For non-2022 methods an empty password (server-level or any client) fails the config.

With a 2022 method and clients: the server method must be a blake3-aes one, every client method must be empty, and if the first client has an address (relay mode) all must have one; violations fail the config.
New spelling of "clients"; v26.3.27 silently ignores it (single-user fallback then demands a server password), and "clients" wins whenever present.
When omitted the inbound accepts TCP only; UDP must be listed explicitly ("tcp,udp").
Also valid inside servers[]; in v26.3.27 it only takes effect with a 2022 method, and from v26.7.28 it is no longer declared and is silently ignored.
Also valid inside servers[]; in v26.3.27 it only takes effect with a 2022 method, and from v26.7.28 it is no longer declared and is silently ignored.
Exactly one server is required, with address, non-zero port and non-empty password; anything else fails the config.
Flat form (address, port, method, password, level, email) replaces "servers" whenever address is set.
Any non-empty flow on a trojan client fails the config ("Flow for Trojan" removed) in every tag.
Any non-empty flow (flat or in servers[]) fails the config in every tag.
New spelling of "clients"; v26.3.27 silently ignores it (inbound loads with zero users), and "clients" wins whenever present.
Each fallback path must be empty or start with "/", dest must be a port, host:port, absolute/@ unix path or "serve-ws-none" unless type is given, and xver must be 0-2; otherwise the config fails.
Exactly one server is required, with address, non-zero port and non-empty password.
Flat form (address, port, password, level, email) replaces "servers" whenever address is set.

From v26.7.28 a trojan outbound whose security is not tls/reality fails unless the server is a private IP or a private/dotless name (lan, local, localhost, internal, home.arpa, test, ...); v26.7.28 checks only the flat "address" form, v26.9.9 also servers[].
New spelling of "clients"; v26.3.27 silently ignores it so the inbound loads with zero users, and "clients" wins whenever present (even empty).
Required in every tag: empty fails with "please add/set decryption:none", and anything that is neither "none" nor a well-formed mlkem768x25519plus string fails.
The mode must be native/xorpub/random, the third part a seconds value or range, and every part of 20+ chars must base64url-decode to 32 or 64 bytes.
fallbacks with decryption other than "none" fail; each fallback also needs a path starting with "/" (or empty), a resolvable dest (unless type is set) and xver 0-2.
Same set for settings.flow (the default for clients without one); exact case, and any other value (including xtls-rprx-vision-udp443 on an inbound) fails the config.
A non-empty encryption on an inbound client fails the config; inbound uses settings.decryption.
An inbound client's reverse needs a non-empty tag and must not carry sniffing; otherwise the config fails.
Users are decoded straight into the protobuf account, so these internal fields are recognised keys, but they are derived from decryption/encryption parsing; never emit them.
id must be a 32-36 char hex UUID or a 1-30 char string (mapped to a UUIDv5); empty, 31 chars or 37+ chars fails the config (same for vnext users[].id).
id must be a 32-36 char hex UUID or a 1-30 char string (mapped to a UUIDv5); empty, 31 chars or 37+ chars fails the config (same for vnext users[].id).
id must be a 32-36 char hex UUID or a 1-30 char string (mapped to a UUIDv5); empty, 31 chars or 37+ chars fails the config (same for vnext users[].id).
id must be a 32-36 char hex UUID or a 1-30 char string (mapped to a UUIDv5); empty, 31 chars or 37+ chars fails the config (same for vnext users[].id).
Required in every tag (flat or vnext users[]): empty fails with "please add/set encryption:none", and a malformed mlkem string fails.
Mode must be native/xorpub/random, the third part exactly 1rtt or 0rtt, and every 20+ char part must base64url-decode to 32 or 1184 bytes.
Exact case; any other value fails the config.
vnext must have exactly one entry with an address and exactly one user; otherwise the config fails.
Flat form (address, port, id, flow, encryption, reverse, level, email, testpre, testseed) replaces "vnext" whenever address is set.
reverse is only allowed in the flat form; inside vnext users it fails the config.
reverse needs a non-empty tag; its optional sniffing uses the normal sniffing validation.
Declared but never used (the assignment is commented out) in all three tags, so it has no effect.

From v26.7.28 a vless outbound with encryption "none" and security not tls/reality fails unless the server is a private IP or private/dotless name; v26.7.28 checks only the flat "address" form, v26.9.9 also vnext.
Case-insensitive; any unlisted value silently becomes auto, so from v26.7.28 "none" and "zero" load but quietly mean auto (same for vnext users[].security).
New spelling of "clients"; v26.3.27 silently ignores it (zero users), and "clients" wins whenever present.
vnext must have exactly one entry with an address and exactly one user; otherwise the config fails.
Flat form (address, port, id, security, experiments, level, email) replaces "vnext" whenever address is set.
alterId is not declared in any tag (user keys are id, security, experiments, level, email), so it is silently ignored.
alterId is not declared in any tag (user keys are id, security, experiments, level, email), so it is silently ignored.
Required; keys (secretKey, peers[].publicKey, peers[].preSharedKey) must be 64 hex chars or base64 (std or URL, padding optional), otherwise the config fails.

Up to v26.9.9: case-insensitive and "" means forceip; the AsIs/UseIP family is not accepted and fails the config. v26.9.30 and v26.10.10 have no such field at all, so the key is silently ignored and nothing validates it.
Must be empty or exactly 3 bytes (JSON array of 0-255 numbers, or a base64 string); any other length fails the config.
Removed in v26.7.28 and silently ignored from then on.
v26.9.9, v26.9.30 and v26.10.10 decode it for inbounds too, but only the client (outbound) side reads it.
From v26.7.28 inbound peers are built as users and carry level/email.
Must be a JSON array of strings (a single comma string fails decoding); each entry must be an IP or CIDR or the core fails to start; default 10.0.0.1 and fd59:7153:2388:b5fd::1.
v26.3.27 only accepts a CIDR entry if it is a host prefix (/32 IPv4, /128 IPv6) and the core fails to start otherwise; from v26.7.28 any prefix length is accepted and only its address part is used.
The Go field has an empty json tag, so an "isClient" key (any case) is decoded and overrides the inbound/outbound mode; the editor must never emit it.
Required; keys (secretKey, peers[].publicKey, peers[].preSharedKey) must be 64 hex chars or base64 (std or URL, padding optional), otherwise the config fails.

Up to v26.9.9: case-insensitive and "" means forceip; the AsIs/UseIP family is not accepted and fails the config. v26.9.30 and v26.10.10 have no such field at all, so the key is silently ignored and nothing validates it.
Must be empty or exactly 3 bytes (JSON array of 0-255 numbers, or a base64 string); any other length fails the config.
Removed in v26.7.28 and silently ignored from then on.

v26.9.9: IP literals or ["local"] (default 1.1.1.1/1.0.0.1 and their IPv6); a non-IP entry panics when the core starts (MustParseAddr). v26.9.30 and v26.10.10: IP literals only: "local" is gone and now panics like any other name.
Decoded from v26.7.28 but only used on the inbound side; no effect on an outbound.
Must be a JSON array of strings (a single comma string fails decoding); each entry must be an IP or CIDR or the core fails to start; default 10.0.0.1 and fd59:7153:2388:b5fd::1.
v26.3.27 only accepts a CIDR entry if it is a host prefix (/32 IPv4, /128 IPv6) and the core fails to start otherwise; from v26.7.28 any prefix length is accepted and only its address part is used.
The Go field has an empty json tag, so an "isClient" key (any case) is decoded and overrides the inbound/outbound mode; the editor must never emit it.
From v26.7.28 the client checks at core start that peers is non-empty and every peer has publicKey and endpoint; v26.3.27 only discovered this on first use.
The tag is "MTU" in v26.3.27 and "mtu" later, but key matching is case-insensitive so either spelling works in every tag; 0/omitted means 1500.
Adapter description (Windows), default "Wintun"; silently ignored in v26.3.27.
JSON array of strings only (a comma string fails decoding); silently ignored in v26.3.27.
JSON array of strings only (a comma string fails decoding); silently ignored in v26.3.27.
JSON array of strings only (a comma string fails decoding); silently ignored in v26.3.27.
"auto" (the default whenever autoSystemRoutingTable is non-empty), an interface name, or "" to disable; silently ignored in v26.3.27.
Entries are CIDR prefixes (e.g. "10.0.0.1/24"), validated only when the core starts; on Windows a bare IP panics via MustParsePrefix.
Default name changed from "xray0" (v26.3.27) to a random free "utun10"-"utun1024" (v26.7.28+).
A tun inbound skips the listen/port validation every other inbound gets, so port may be omitted in every tag.
